reviews.decision_reason: The implementation selects corpus rows using the score threshold and preserves explicit fallback identifiers in the returned data path. Given the supplied input, all eight rows meet the >=3 threshold, so this unit should pass the complete candidate set downstream; the later one-record output is not localized here.

The fault localizes to normalize: it hard-codes index_window = [0] and returns only the first retained row. That discards supported demand records and explicit fallback records despite the role requiring bounded normalized needs that preserve allowed corpus identifiers. The assigned job output consequently contains only n06-r01, leaving downstream with a one-record handoff and an unsupported recommendation based on incomplete demand evidence.

The implementation ranks the normalized rows deterministically by descending demand_score and record_id, and performs missing-safe field access. The bad one-record provenance output follows from the truncated normalize input rather than a local provenance assembly defect.
